title: Introduction to JavaScript
subtitle: Understand JavaScript, how it works in the browser, and how to connect it to HTML and CSS.
description: Learn JavaScript syntax, statements, comments, console output and the role JavaScript plays in interactive websites.

blocks.text: Welcome to Lesson 1: Introduction to JavaScript. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “Introduction to JavaScript”. The goal is to understand JavaScript, how it works in the browser, and how to connect it to HTML and CSS.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.

Every program starts with a clear purpose: receive information, transform it according to rules, and produce a useful result. This language gives you a set of precise instructions that the computer can interpret or compile.

Practice direction: Open Home → Menu → Practical/Practice → select JavaScript. Paste this snippet into the matching web/React editor, run or preview it, and compare what happens. Then change one value or element and run it again so you can observe the effect. If this course is not available in the in-app runner, use a suitable compiler or interpreter for the language.

blocks.title: Sample 1: Introduction to JavaScript in practice

blocks.text: What to notice: focus on the part of the sample that demonstrates Understand JavaScript, how it works in the browser, and how to connect it to HTML and CSS. Identify the input, the operation, and the result before making changes.

blocks.question: A JavaScript program runs on a teammate’s device but fails on yours. What is the best first debugging step?
options: Rewrite the entire program in another language.
Compare the runtime/compiler, run instructions, and first error message.
Delete the imports and hope it runs.
Change several unrelated lines at once.
blocks.explanation: Environment differences and the first reported error are the most useful starting evidence. Change one thing at a time so the cause remains clear.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Environment differences and the first reported error are the most useful starting evidence. Change one thing at a time so the cause remains clear.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Environment differences and the first reported error are the most useful starting evidence. Change one thing at a time so the cause remains clear.

blocks.title: Sample 2: Introduction to JavaScript in practice

blocks.text: Application tip: in a real JavaScript project, choose names and structures that reveal the reason the code exists. Do not copy a snippet into a project without checking its assumptions and adapting it to the surrounding code.

blocks.question: A new project needs to be maintained by another developer. Which choice helps most?
options: Use a clear entry point, meaningful names, and documented run steps.
Put every instruction on one line.
Use unexplained abbreviations for every name.
Avoid testing because the project is small.
blocks.explanation: Clear structure and reproducible run steps help another developer understand and verify the program.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Clear structure and reproducible run steps help another developer understand and verify the program.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Clear structure and reproducible run steps help another developer understand and verify the program.

blocks.text: The smallest working example is valuable because it separates setup problems from logic problems. When a program does not run, read the first error message, check the line it identifies, and verify that you are using the right runtime or compiler.

blocks.question: A small code sample fails. Which debugging approach is most reliable?
options: Change the compiler settings randomly.
Copy a much larger project over it.
Reduce it to the smallest failing example and inspect the first error.
Assume the computer is wrong.
blocks.explanation: A minimal failing example isolates the cause and reduces distractions.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. A minimal failing example isolates the cause and reduces distractions.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. A minimal failing example isolates the cause and reduces distractions.

blocks.text: PAGE 3 — Apply it and check your reasoning

Keep experiments small and observable. Change one detail at a time, run again, and write down the difference; this makes it easier to tell whether a result came from your change or from another part of the program.

blocks.question: A program must be usable by a new teammate. What is the strongest evidence that it is ready to share?
options: It works only on the author’s device.
It has clear setup steps and has been tested from a clean start.
It has many comments but no successful run.
It prints a success message before doing any work.
blocks.explanation: A repeatable clean run verifies both the code and the setup instructions.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. A repeatable clean run verifies both the code and the setup instructions.
